summary: Significant organised local and city-wide opposition at pre-application stage. A local residents' campaign (Hermiston Data Centre Campaign) and a Change.org petition (3,581 signatures by July 2026) oppose the scheme; APRS campaigns against it nationally; the Cockburn Association questions 'green' claims without opposing data centres outright. The February 2026 refusal of the nearby South Gyle data centre and the council Planning Committee's June 2026 call for a Scottish Government moratorium on large-scale data centres form the political backdrop. Following a third-party request, Scottish Ministers directed on 17 August 2026 that an Environmental Impact Assessment is required. The PAN was notified to Currie and Ratho Community Councils, Pentland Hills ward councillors, Gordon MacDonald MSP and Dr Scott Arthur MP; formal representations will only be counted once an application is submitted.

principal_concerns.concern: Permanent loss of productive prime agricultural Green Belt land in the Gogar Special Landscape Area
principal_concerns.raised_by: Change.org petition (Gordon Fraser); Hermiston Data Centre Campaign; APRS

principal_concerns.concern: Lack of transparency on water/cooling requirements, supply arrangements and drought resilience
Scale of electricity demand (200 MW), grid capacity and cumulative effects with other Scottish data centre proposals; diversion of renewable generation
Generator testing, noise, air quality and lighting impacts on nearby homes and schools
principal_concerns.developer_response: Council PAN report requires demonstration of no significant impact on residential amenity (noise, air quality, light)

principal_concerns.concern: Impact on the Union Canal corridor (scheduled monument) and its recreational and biodiversity value, plus Hermiston Conservation Area and listed buildings
principal_concerns.raised_by: Change.org petition; identified as key heritage issues by council officers

principal_concerns.concern: Absence of a national definition of a 'green data centre' and of a named hyperscale tenant; the council initially concluded EIA was not required, but Scottish Ministers directed on 17 August 2026 that an EIA is required

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: £1.4bn investment, local construction spend and GVA claims (see economic_claims.json)
Community funds for play areas, youth/skills programmes, wellbeing, green space and social enterprises, managed with the council and an independent delivery partner
Potential future waste-heat export to a district heating network serving the Heriot-Watt area

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: Hermiston Data Centre Campaign (spokesperson Sarah Matthews)
stakeholder_positions.position: Opposes the hyperscale data centre on greenfield land; petition reported at over 2,000 signatures in earlier coverage
Opposes; campaigns for an immediate Scottish Government moratorium on hyperscale data centre applications
Not categorically opposed to data centres; calls for a clear national definition of a genuinely 'green' data centre, robust evidence, brownfield preference and landscape integration standards

stakeholder_positions.stakeholder: City of Edinburgh Council Planning Committee
stakeholder_positions.position: In June 2026 requested that the Scottish Government introduce a moratorium on large-scale data centres until clearer national guidance on 'green data centre' definitions emerges
Directed on 17 August 2026 that an Environmental Impact Assessment is required for the Wester Hermiston proposal (EIA-230-002).

notes: Two Change.org petitions exist ('Stop development of mega data centre Wester Hermiston' by Gordon Fraser, 3,581 signatures; and 'STOP Hyperscale AI DATA CENTRE at Hermiston, Edinburgh'). Formal objection counts will only be available once a planning application is validated and open for representations.
